CFTC investigates if Kalshi improperly self-certified event contracts
headlines.summary: News of the probe comes after the CFTC ordered Kalshi to take down a sports-related "mention markets" back in August.
headlines.article_text: CFTC investigates if Kalshi improperly self-certified event contracts Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Kalshi called it a minor issue in how the contracts were filed and said it is working with the CFTC to address the matter. Prediction market platforms are allowed to self-certify event contracts without the federal agency's approval, as long as they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act. A Kalshi billboard displaying US Congress midterm election odds in New York, US, on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. Angelina Katsanis | Bloomberg | Getty Images The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether prediction market platform Kalshi failed to properly inform the agency of proposed event contracts, Kalshi confirmed to CNBC. Kalshi called it a minor issue in how the contracts were filed and said it is working with the CFTC to address the matter. The CFTC flagged weather-related contracts, Kalshi said. The leading prediction market platform didn't say when the agency began investigating Kalshi. The CFTC didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Politico first reported on the probe on Tuesday, noting charges could happen soon, based on the CFTC's private notification to Kalshi. The platform declined to comment on any possible charges. Prediction market platforms are allowed to self-certify event contracts without the federal agency's prior approval, as long as they comply with the Commodity Exchange Act. The self-certification allows for faster introduction of new contracts. 'Procedural error' "The notice is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren't live," said Elisabeth Diana, head of communications at Kalshi. "We are already addressing the issue." The move is the latest by the CFTC as it seeks to rein in prediction markets, which face growing scrutiny in Washington from regulators and members of Congress . In August, the CFTC ordered Kalshi to take down sports-related " mention markets " — where speculators can trade on what individuals will say in a broadcast or speech — while it looked into the event contract type. The agency is also conducting a broad probe into competitor Polymarket , which includes reviewing if the company violated a 2022 settlement with the CFTC to prohibit U.S. traders from accessing its international trading platform. Polymarket's domestic exchange operates separately from the global platform. Prediction markets are also expected to face heightened scrutiny once the Democratic Congress is sworn into office in January. Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., in a Tuesday social media post on X , called for a ban on sports prediction markets — which account for the overwhelming majority of volume on leading platforms. Leila Navidi | Star Tribune | Getty Images U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his Washington home to a military base for his safety amid growing Iranian threats against him. Bessent's move, first reported by The New York Times and confirmed to CNBC by a person familiar with the situation, came as the U.S. war against Iran remains locked in an uneasy stalemate punctuated by intermittent fighting. Concerns about Bessent's security were heightened after The Wall Street Journal "published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located," the person told CNBC on condition of anonymity to discuss the nonpublicized move. The Journal published an aerial view of Bessent's $12.5 million Georgetown mansion in late January 2025, shortly after he bought it. Those security concerns have forced Bessent "to relocate to a military base for his safety," the person said, admonishing the news media to "act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials." Wall Street Journal publisher Dow Jones did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on the person's statement. The Times reported that U.S. officials have recently seen Iran's plots against American targets reach a more advanced stage and that Bessent's leading role in the ongoing U.S.-Iran war has made him a top target. Bessent has led Operation Economic Outcast, a Treasury campaign launched in August to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and other financial measures, in addition to the U.S. military actions. A Treasury Department spokesperson told CNBC that Bessent "will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats." The Cabinet secretary "remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran's economy," the spokesperson added. Bessent's move comes as the Department of Justice said late Tuesday that three Iranian nationals had been indicted on terrorism-related charges. The department said the three were allegedly involved in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States. The alleged plots included an attack in September targeting the British Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, England, where U.S. military personnel were stationed. "Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American service members will be prosecuted by the United States government," Attorney General Todd Blanche said. Earlier in October , British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Iran was involved in the incident at RAF Fairford that led to the arrest of five men on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi then rejected the allegation, writing on X that Burnham was "barking up the wrong tree." RAF Fairford, in Gloucestershire, is a key U.S. Air Force operating location in Europe and has supported deployments of American strategic bombers and other aircraft. The Journal reported Monday that the U.S. evacuated its aircraft from another RAF base in England following a threat from Iran. Stalled negotiations Separately, Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly said military action against Iran may not be necessary if economic sanctions and Washington's naval blockade are working. On Monday , President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that "Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and others, would prefer the status quo, in other words, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History." "We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict," Trump added. Asked Tuesday why he would not simply declare an end to the Iran war, Trump said he wanted to ensure that U.S. allies in the region were "not hurt" and that there was a "long-term solution. However, Iranian officials have denied that negotiations are underway. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said claims that talks were continuing were aimed at "easing economic pressures and reducing oil prices." Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude prices edged higher during Wednesday's Asia trading session, at about $92 and $86 per barrel, respectively. — CNBC's Eamon Javers contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: CoreWeave stock soars as CEO reaffirms AI compute demand Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave posted quarterly revenue that beat estimates and raised its full-year guidance. Neoclouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have come under scrutiny this month as investors assessed the sustainability of the AI trade. In this article I1V-DE IREN APLD NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 3:59 03:59 CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator: The demand for computing infrastructure remains overwhelming Squawk on the Street CoreWeave shares jumped 23% Wednesday after the neocloud posted quarterly earnings that beat estimates and raised its guidance for the year. "Demand for the infrastructure is and remains overwhelming." CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Wednesday. "I think I said that we are 10x oversubscribed to the existing capacity that we have left in 2027, and we are multiples ... oversubscribed on the capacity we have out in 2028," he said. Neoclouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have come under scrutiny this month as investors assessed the sustainability of the AI trade. CoreWeave, in particular, sparked alarm when spreads on its CDS widened past 11% , generally viewed as a distress level, as investors have to pay up for protection against default. With the price of its high-yield debt climbing, CoreWeave highlighted additional routes to finance its data center build-out with less alarming yields, quelling investor concerns for the time being. "Our asset level debt has basically been rock solid through this entire thing," Intrator told CNBC. "There is an enormous demand for that product. We're about to launch another asset-level debt in the next week or two that has already been rated high investment grade." Intrator added that he expects it "will be underwritten in the market at 7% to 7.5% interest," which will bring down the average weighted cost of capital for the company. CoreWeave shares this year. The three months to Sept. 30 marked a "breakout quarter" for CoreWeave, Intrator said on the conference call, adding that growth was supported by multiple sources of funding, including financing backed by customer contracts and around $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits. Revenue jumped 168% to $3.7 billion in the third quarter, the company said in a Tuesday statement . Other neclouds also rose on CoreWeave's strong results, with Nebius up 17%, Applied Digital up 9% and Iren up 8% after the open. Despite fears that a "blue wave" in last week's midterm elections could restrict data center capacity, Intrator reiterated that data center growth looks poised to continue as expected for CoreWeave. "We don't see any impact on our ability to deliver the data centers within the U.S. that are required for us to deliver on our backlog," Intrator told CNBC on Wednesday. "In Texas, Governor-elect [Gina Hinojosa], said that facilities that are permitted and under construction will continue, and we've been really, really thoughtful about the broad distribution." CoreWeave expects $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion in adjusted operating income on $13 billion to $13.3 billion in revenue. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha were looking for $1.07 billion in adjusted operating income, and analysts polled by LSEG had expected $12.86 billion in 2026 revenue. The neocloud has done well to allay concerns about financing by moving away from unsecured bond financing, Zacks Chief Equity Strategist John Blank told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe." "It might be the bottom for CoreWeave," Blank said Wednesday. "But the shares are so beaten up, you have to believe at this point there's more value on the upside than the down." headlines.article_text: CoreWeave CEO cancels planned share sale program Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said Wednesday that he has canceled his 10b5 stock sale plan. Intrator has sold 8.26 million shares at an average price of $96.14 per share for a total of $794.2 million under his most recent plan. The neocloud beat on revenue in Q3 and upped its forecast, while Intrator indicated the company will be fine despite last week's Democratic midterm sweep. In this article I1V-DE Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Michael Intrator, co-founder and chief executive officer of CoreWeave Inc., at the Bloomberg Tech summit in London, UK, on Tuesday, Oct. 21, 2025. Chris J. Ratcliffe | Bloomberg | Getty Images CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC on Wednesday that he has canceled his 10b5 stock sale plan after the company reported strong revenue growth and beat Q3 expectations . "Until there is a material change in in, in our equity pricing, my 10b5 has been sidelined," he told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." He said any further selling would be "just normal tax stuff." Under Intrator's 10b5-1 plan announced in November 2025, the CEO has sold 8.26 million shares at an average price of $96.14 per share for a total of $794.2 million. Intrator and his co-founders have faced criticism for their stock sales as the company's stock has struggled, with shares down 18% so far in 2026 despite a 20% post-earnings rally on Wednesday. The company has faced further pressure from the sell-off in the aftermath of last week's sweeping electoral victory for Democrats, but Intrator told investors on the earnings call that the company isn't worried about the political changes on the horizon. "We do not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift that's occurred," Intrator said on his company's earnings call late Tuesday, in response to a question about new pressures after the election. "We believe that what has occurred is a statement around how you build. We want to build responsibly." Intrator's comments came after CoreWeave reported 168% year-over-year revenue growth, beating estimates, and lifted its forecast for 2026. The stock rallied in extended trading, as the report offered some relief to investors, who have pushed the shares down about 27% over the past month. In the Nov. 3 midterm elections, voters sided in favor of greater restrictions on data centers in 40 out of 41 ballot measures in 10 states, according to Ballotpedia . Democrats won control of both houses of Congress and were victorious in governors' races in critical AI infrastructure states like Texas, Ohio and Georgia. In each state, the winning candidate favors some restrictions on new data centers. J.P. Morgan Asset Management wrote in a report after the election that data center projects from 2028 onward are "most exposed," and "face greater uncertainty around permitting, power availability and financing." But CoreWeave says it's not slowing down. The company said it still anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026, and it's now targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures, implying 155% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha were looking for $37.69 billion. "We are very comfortable with our pipeline," Intrator said, adding that the message from voters isn't a deterrent because the company is always conscious about "being good neighbors." "We think that that is an opportunity for us to continue to scale our business within the new political reality that exists," Intrator said. —CNBC's Nick Wells contributed to this article.
